title: Amazon DynamoDB global tables now support disassociating replicas
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with Amazon DynamoDB global tables now support disassociating replicas
body_markdown:
[Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Introduction.html) global tables now support disassociating a replica without deleting its table or data. Global tables provide fully managed, multi-Region, multi-active replication. You can now stop replication to and from a replica and continue using the same table as a single-Region table.


An account can leave a shared multi-account global table and continue using its table independently. You can also stop replication to a Region while keeping its table for local workloads, validation, or audit, without creating a replacement table or copying data.


DynamoDB supports disassociating replicas in all AWS Regions for same-account and multi-account global tables that use multi-Region eventual consistency (MREC).


To get started, use the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, DynamoDB API, or AWS CloudFormation. For more information, see[Disassociating replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/globaltables-disassociate.html) in the Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide.
